transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because I’m having a hard time keeping things organized. There are too many moving parts at work—patent notes, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, team decisions—and I keep ending up doing whatever feels most urgent or loudest, not necessarily what actually matters. It’s gotten hard to manage.
Are these difficulties with organization and prioritization causing you a lot of stress or problems in your daily life?

Yes. It’s… it’s starting to cause real problems. I missed a checkpoint for a patent filing, and after a rough architecture review, some collaborators seemed to be questioning whether I can actually lead the bigger project. So, yeah, it’s affecting my reputation at work.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless, like you can't sit still?

Yeah… somewhat. On longer design calls especially, I get this sort of pressure to get up. I’ll pace around my office or switch chairs a lot, even when I’m trying to look like I’m sitting still and paying attention.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?
Not really, no. I mean… I might make quick calls sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I often act without thinking.
Do you often find yourself easily distracted by things around you?

Yes. It doesn’t take much. A Slack ping, a tab flashing… sometimes even just an idea popping into my head, and I’ve lost the thread of what I was coding. Then I realize I’ve spent twenty minutes down some unrelated design path.
Do you have mood swings?
Not really sure. I mean, I get frustrated sometimes, but I wouldn’t call it mood swings exactly.
Do you ever find yourself so focused on a task that you lose track of everything else around you?
I’m not sure. I can get absorbed in something, I guess, but I don’t know that I’d say I lose track of everything around me.
Do you often struggle to finish tasks once you've started them?
I’m not really sure. Sometimes I leave things half-done, but I don’t know if it’s more than most people.
Do you often find yourself talking excessively?
Not really, I don’t think so. I’m usually pretty quiet unless I need to say something.
Do you have trouble waiting for your turn in lines or when speaking with others?
Not really, no. Lines are annoying, but I don’t think I have a particular problem waiting. In conversations… I usually just wait.
Do you ever become so absorbed in an activity that you forget to eat, sleep, or take breaks?
I’m not sure. I can get focused on something for a while, especially work stuff, but I don’t know that I forget to eat or sleep because of it.
Do you ever become so focused on a task that you lose track of time?
I mean… sometimes, I guess. If I’m working on something, I can look up and realize more time passed than I thought. But I don’t know if that’s unusual.
Do you ever become so focused on a task that you can't stop thinking about it, even when you're not working on it?
I don’t know… not really in a way I’d call a problem. Sometimes something from work stays in the back of my mind, but I can usually leave it alone.
Have you noticed any difficulties in your personal relationships due to your organizational issues or other symptoms you've mentioned?
Not really… I mean, nothing I’d clearly point to as a relationship problem. Maybe people get a little annoyed if I’m disorganized, but I haven’t really thought of it that way.
Do you ever find yourself so intensely focused on something that it's hard for you to shift your attention away from it?
Not really… I mean, I can get into something for a while, but I don’t think I get stuck on it like that. At least, I haven’t really noticed it.
Have you experienced any strain in your friendships or romantic relationships as a result of your difficulties with organization and focus?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really connected it to that. I guess maybe small frustrations here and there, but I wouldn’t say it’s caused real strain that I’ve noticed.
Have your organizational issues and difficulties with focus significantly impacted your ability to perform your job or maintain your overall well-being?

Yeah… work, definitely. I don’t love saying that, but it’s starting to affect how people see me there.

I missed a checkpoint for a patent filing, and there was this architecture review that didn’t go well. It was pretty difficult, and afterward I got the sense that some collaborators were questioning whether I should be leading the bigger project. So… yeah, it’s not just in my head at this point.
Do you ever become so focused on a task that you can't think about anything else?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I can get absorbed in something if it’s interesting, but not to the point where I can’t think about anything else. At least… not that I’ve noticed.
Do you ever find yourself so focused on a task that you can't stop thinking about it even when you're trying to do something else?
Not really. I mean, if something’s unresolved it can sit in the back of my mind, but I wouldn’t say I’m stuck thinking about it when I’m trying to do something else.
Do you ever become so focused on a task that you tune out everything else around you?
Not really, no. I mean, I can be engaged in something, but I don’t think I tune out everything around me like that.
